createdBy: claude (found while sampling real zug tail output for landing copy)
impact:
Five of 180 records in observations.jsonl have the remainder of the caller's tool-call block serialised into the `observation` string value. Affected lines 176-180, all dated 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21. Observed leaked fragments: `</observation>`, `<parameter name="pattern">` followed by the pattern text, and in the newest record `</invoke>`.

Reproduce: `zug tail 2` renders the garbage inline, e.g. a record ending `...experimental discipline (...).</observation>\n</invoke>` and another ending `...retained with the axis they failed on.</observation>\n<parameter name="pattern">converges by accumulating rejection criteria`.

Correlation worth checking first: every affected record is a call that also supplied the optional `pattern` argument, and all five are recent. That points at argument serialisation on the client side rather than at storage, but Zug is where the damage lands and where it can be caught.

Why it matters beyond cosmetics: observations.jsonl is the input to synthesis. src/synthesize.ts feeds these strings into the PERSONA and PLAYBOOK prompts, so the model is being shown XML-ish tool-call fragments as if they were content. That risks the model echoing markup back into PERSONA.md, and it inflates the token cost of every synthesis. It also corrupts recurrence matching if the trailing text lands in the value used for pattern comparison.

Suggested fix: validate and strip in zug_save_observation before append. Reject or trim anything from the first `</observation>`, `<parameter`, `</invoke>` or `</` onward, and consider failing loudly rather than silently storing, so a malformed caller is visible instead of quietly polluting the corpus. A one-off repair pass over the five existing records is also needed; they are already in the synthesis input.
resolution:
Client-side fix committed (371ac20). Local corpus repaired. NOT fully closed: the canonical server still holds the corrupt records.

**What shipped**

`stripToolCallMarkup` / `sanitizeObservation` in src/storage.ts, applied in both write paths: `appendObservation` and `addObservations` (the sync merge). Truncates at the first marker rather than deleting matches, since the leak is always a tail. A record consisting only of markup is left intact rather than emptied, because truncation cannot repair it and a silent empty string is worse than a visible bad one.

`zug_save_observation` now appends a warning to its response when it strips, so a malformed caller is told instead of being quietly cleaned up after.

`zug repair [--dry-run]` added and documented in the README CLI block (a packaging test enforces that every dispatched command is documented).

**Why the merge path mattered more than it looked**

Dedupe is on `timestamp|observation`. A repaired local record would no longer have matched its corrupt twin arriving from the server, so a pull would have appended both and a push would have sent the repaired one as an additional row. Repairing locally on a synced install would have doubled every record it fixed. Sanitizing on ingest makes the two compare equal so dedupe drops the bad one. There is a test named for exactly this.

**Applied locally**

Backed up to `~/.zug/observations.jsonl.pre-iss057-20260920222206` first. 180 scanned, 5 repaired, 180 records still present afterwards, zero markup remaining, `zug tail` reads clean.

**Still open: the canonical server**

This install is synced (`~/.zug/config` exists), so the authoritative log lives on Fly and still contains the five corrupt records. Synthesis runs server-side, which means the PERSONA prompt is still being fed the markup. Closing this requires:

1. Deploy the fix so the server sanitizes on ingest.
2. Run `zug repair` where the canonical store lives (fly ssh console), or equivalent.

Local pulls will no longer reintroduce the corruption in the meantime, because ingest sanitizes, so the local corpus stays clean either way. The remaining exposure is synthesis quality on the server.

**Root cause not addressed**

This fixes the damage, not the leak. Every affected call also passed `pattern`, and all five landed within about 30 hours, which suggests a client-side argument-serialisation issue rather than anything in Zug. Worth noting: writing these marker strings literally into a tool call reproduces the truncation, which is how the shape was confirmed.
title: zug_save_observation stores trailing tool-call markup inside the observation text
